title: Mathlib Graph Theory Imports
content: Imports `SimpleGraph.Basic` for the graph type, `SimpleGraph.Clique` for clique/triangle definitions, `Fintype` for finiteness, and `Tactic` for proof automation. The `Sym2` type from SimpleGraph represents unordered edges.
mathContext: Mathlib's `SimpleGraph V` models simple undirected graphs as symmetric irreflexive relations on vertex type $V$. Edges are represented as elements of `Sym2 V` (unordered pairs).

title: Triangle (IsTriangle)
content: A triangle in graph $G$ is a triple of distinct, pairwise-adjacent vertices. The definition requires all three distinctness conditions and all three adjacencies explicitly, making it compatible with Lean's definitional equality.
mathContext:
A triangle is a complete subgraph $K_3$: vertices $a, b, c$ with $a 
e b$, $b 
e c$, $a 
e c$, and edges $\{a,b\}, \{b,c\}, \{a,c\} \in E(G)$.

title: Hits Triangle
content: An edge set $S$ hits a triangle $abc$ if $S$ contains at least one of the triangle's three edges. This is the fundamental notion for defining triangle edge covers—an edge set that hits every triangle in the graph.
mathContext: $S$ hits triangle $(a,b,c)$ iff $\{a,b\} \in S \lor \{b,c\} \in S \lor \{a,c\} \in S$. This is the hypergraph transversal condition where triangles form a 3-uniform hypergraph on the edge set.

title: Triangle Edge Cover
content: A triangle edge cover is an edge set that hits every triangle in $G$. This is the edge analogue of a vertex cover for the triangle hypergraph. The minimum such cover has size $\tau_1(G)$.
mathContext: $S$ is a triangle edge cover iff $\forall (a,b,c)$ forming a triangle in $G$, $S \cap \{\{a,b\},\{b,c\},\{a,c\}\} \ne \emptyset$. Equivalently, $S$ is a transversal of the triangle hypergraph $\mathcal{H} = (E(G), \{E(T) : T \text{ is a triangle}\})$.

title: Triangle-Sparse Edge Set
content: An edge set is triangle-sparse if no triangle has two or more of its edges in the set. This is the independence condition dual to covering: a maximum triangle-sparse set has size $\alpha_1(G)$.
mathContext: $S$ is triangle-sparse iff for every triangle $(a,b,c)$, $|S \cap \{\{a,b\},\{b,c\},\{a,c\}\}| \le 1$. This is equivalent to $S$ being an independent set in the triangle hypergraph $\mathcal{H}$.

title: Bipartite Graph
content: A graph is bipartite if it admits a proper 2-coloring: a function $f: V \to \{0,1\}$ such that adjacent vertices receive different colors. Equivalently, the graph contains no odd cycles.
mathContext: $G$ is bipartite iff $\exists f: V \to \mathrm{Bool}$ such that $G.\mathrm{Adj}(v,w) \implies f(v) \ne f(w)$. By König's theorem, this is equivalent to $\chi(G) \le 2$, or equivalently, $G$ contains no odd cycle.

title: Full Edge Set is a Cover
content: The full edge set $E(G)$ is always a triangle edge cover: every triangle has all three of its edges in $E(G)$ by definition. This establishes well-definedness of $\tau_1$ (the infimum is over a non-empty set).
mathContext: $E(G)$ is a triangle edge cover since for any triangle $(a,b,c)$, $\{a,b\} \in E(G)$ by adjacency. Thus $\tau_1(G) \le |E(G)|$.

title: Empty Set is Sparse
content: The empty edge set is vacuously triangle-sparse: no triangle can have two edges in $\emptyset$. This establishes well-definedness of $\alpha_1$ (the supremum is over a non-empty set, since $\emptyset$ is always feasible).
mathContext: $\emptyset$ is triangle-sparse since $|\emptyset \cap E(T)| = 0 \le 1$ for every triangle $T$. Thus $\alpha_1(G) \ge 0$.

title: τ₁(G): Triangle Edge Cover Number
content: Defined as the minimum cardinality over all triangle edge covers that are subsets of $E(G)$, using `Finset.inf'`. The witness for non-emptiness is the full edge set (from `edgeFinset_is_cover`). This is the covering number of the triangle hypergraph.
mathContext: $\tau_1(G) = \min\{|S| : S \subseteq E(G),\, S \text{ is a triangle edge cover}\}$. This is the transversal number $\tau(\mathcal{H})$ of the triangle hypergraph $\mathcal{H}$.

title: α₁(G): Triangle-Sparse Number
content: Defined as the maximum cardinality over all triangle-sparse subsets of $E(G)$, using `Finset.sup'`. The witness for non-emptiness is the empty set (from `empty_is_sparse`). This is the independence number of the triangle hypergraph.
mathContext: $\alpha_1(G) = \max\{|S| : S \subseteq E(G),\, S \text{ is triangle-sparse}\}$. This is the independence number $\alpha(\mathcal{H})$ of the triangle hypergraph.

title: τ_B(G): Bipartite Edge Deletion Number
content: Axiomatized as the minimum number of edges whose removal makes $G$ bipartite. This is the odd cycle edge transversal number. A full definition would require Mathlib's `deleteEdges` and a proof that bipartiteness is witnessed by some edge set removal.
mathContext: $\tau_B(G) = \min\{|S| : S \subseteq E(G),\, G - S \text{ is bipartite}\}$. This equals the minimum edge cut to eliminate all odd cycles. By the max-flow min-cut theorem for odd cycles, this relates to fractional chromatic number.

title: Bipartite Implies Triangle-Free
content:
Bipartite graphs contain no triangles. The proof uses a pigeonhole argument: in a 2-coloring $f: V 	o \mathrm{Bool}$, edges connect differently-colored vertices. Three mutual adjacencies $a$-$b$, $b$-$c$, $a$-$c$ force $f(a) 
e f(b)$, $f(b) 
e f(c)$, hence $f(a) = f(c)$, contradicting $f(a) 
e f(c)$. The proof uses `cases` on `Bool` values and `simp_all`.
mathContext:
If $G$ is bipartite with 2-coloring $f$, then $G$ has no triangle, since a triangle on $\{a,b,c\}$ requires $f(a) 
e f(b) 
e f(c) 
e f(a)$, impossible with $|\mathrm{Bool}| = 2$. This is the contrapositive of: graphs with odd cycles are not 2-colorable.

title: τ₁ ≤ τ_B: Covers from Bipartite Removal
content: Any edge set whose removal makes $G$ bipartite is automatically a triangle edge cover (since bipartite graphs are triangle-free). Therefore the minimum triangle cover is at most the minimum bipartite-making removal. This inequality is the bridge between the original EGT conjecture and Norin-Sun's stronger result.
mathContext: $\tau_1(G) \le \tau_B(G)$ because if $G - S$ is bipartite (hence triangle-free), then $S$ must contain at least one edge from every triangle of $G$. This is the key reduction: bounding $\alpha_1 + \tau_B$ suffices for bounding $\alpha_1 + \tau_1$.

title: EGT Conjecture
content: The Erdős-Gallai-Tuza conjecture: $\alpha_1(G) + \tau_1(G) \le n^2/4$ for every graph $G$ on $n$ vertices. The bound $n^2/4$ matches Mantel's theorem and Turán's theorem for triangles.
mathContext: $\alpha_1(G) + \tau_1(G) \le \frac{n^2}{4}$ where $n = |V(G)|$. The bound is tight: balanced complete bipartite graphs $K_{\lfloor n/2 \rfloor, \lceil n/2 \rceil}$ achieve $\alpha_1 + \tau_1 = \lfloor n^2/4 \rfloor$.

title: Norin-Sun 2016: The Stronger Result
content: Axiomatizes the Norin-Sun theorem: $\alpha_1(G) + \tau_B(G) \le n^2/4$. This is strictly stronger than the EGT conjecture since $\tau_B \ge \tau_1$. The proof, which uses structural graph theory and the Kruskal-Katona theorem, is beyond current Mathlib.
mathContext: $\alpha_1(G) + \tau_B(G) \le \frac{n^2}{4}$ (Norin-Sun 2016). Since $\tau_1 \le \tau_B$, this implies $\alpha_1 + \tau_1 \le \alpha_1 + \tau_B \le n^2/4$.

title: EGT Conjecture Resolved
content: The main theorem: the EGT conjecture follows from Norin-Sun and $\tau_1 \le \tau_B$. The proof unfolds both definitions, applies Norin-Sun, casts the natural number inequality $\tau_1 \le \tau_B$ to reals via `Nat.cast_le`, and closes with `linarith`. This is the formal derivation showing the original conjecture is a corollary of the stronger result.
mathContext: $\alpha_1 + \tau_1 \le \alpha_1 + \tau_B \le n^2/4$ by monotonicity and Norin-Sun. The `linarith` tactic handles the real arithmetic chain.

title: τ₁ = 0 for Triangle-Free Graphs
content: For triangle-free graphs, the empty set is a valid triangle edge cover (vacuously), so $\tau_1(G) = 0$. The proof uses `le_antisymm`: the empty set witnesses $\tau_1 \le 0$ via `Finset.inf'_le`, and $0 \le \tau_1$ is trivial.
mathContext: If $G$ has no triangles, then $\tau_1(G) = 0$, since $\emptyset$ is a triangle edge cover (vacuously hitting all zero triangles).

title: α₁ = |E(G)| for Triangle-Free Graphs
content: For triangle-free graphs, every edge set is vacuously triangle-sparse, so the maximum sparse set is the full edge set. The proof shows both $\alpha_1 \le |E|$ (all sparse sets are subsets of edges) and $\alpha_1 \ge |E|$ (the full edge set is sparse).
mathContext: If $G$ is triangle-free, $\alpha_1(G) = |E(G)|$, since every subset of $E(G)$ is trivially triangle-sparse (no triangle exists to violate the sparsity condition).

title: Mantel's Theorem (1907)
content: Axiomatizes Mantel's theorem: a triangle-free graph on $n$ vertices has at most $n^2/4$ edges. This classical result (the first case of Turán's theorem) is the baseline for the triangle-free reduction of the EGT conjecture.
mathContext: Mantel (1907): If $G$ is triangle-free on $n$ vertices, $|E(G)| \le \lfloor n^2/4 \rfloor$. Equality iff $G \cong K_{\lfloor n/2 \rfloor, \lceil n/2 \rceil}$. This is Turán's theorem for $r = 2$: $\mathrm{ex}(n, K_3) = \lfloor n^2/4 \rfloor$.

title: Triangle-Free EGT via Mantel
content: For triangle-free graphs, the EGT conjecture reduces to Mantel's theorem: $\alpha_1 + \tau_1 = |E| + 0 = |E| \le n^2/4$. The proof rewrites using `triangle_free_tau1_zero` and `triangle_free_alpha1_all_edges`, then applies Mantel.
mathContext: Triangle-free case: $\alpha_1(G) + \tau_1(G) = |E(G)| + 0 = |E(G)| \le n^2/4$ by Mantel. This shows the EGT bound is tight for triangle-free graphs when $G = K_{\lfloor n/2 \rfloor, \lceil n/2 \rceil}$.

title: Basic Upper Bounds
content: Proves $\tau_1(G) \le |E(G)|$ (the full edge set is a cover) and $\alpha_1(G) \le |E(G)|$ (sparse sets are subsets of edges). These follow directly from the definitions using `Finset.inf'_le` and `Finset.sup'_le` respectively.
mathContext: $\tau_1(G) \le |E(G)|$ and $\alpha_1(G) \le |E(G)|$ are trivial bounds. The interesting bound is $\alpha_1(G) \le n^2/4$ (from Norin-Sun).

title: α₁(G) ≤ n²/4 from Norin-Sun
content: Derives $\alpha_1(G) \le n^2/4$ as a corollary of Norin-Sun by observing $\tau_B \ge 0$. Since $\alpha_1 + \tau_B \le n^2/4$ and $\tau_B \ge 0$, we get $\alpha_1 \le n^2/4$. Uses `Nat.cast_nonneg` and `linarith`.
mathContext: $\alpha_1(G) \le \alpha_1(G) + \tau_B(G) \le n^2/4$ since $\tau_B(G) \ge 0$. This gives an independent bound on the triangle-sparse number without involving the covering number.

title: Triangle-Free Sum Identity
content: For triangle-free graphs, $\alpha_1(G) + \tau_1(G) = |E(G)|$. This is a Gallai-type identity for the triangle hypergraph in the degenerate case: when there are no triangles, covering and independence partition the edge count exactly.
mathContext: $\alpha_1(G) + \tau_1(G) = |E(G)| + 0 = |E(G)|$ for triangle-free $G$. Compare with the Gallai identity $\alpha(G) + \tau(G) = n$ for vertex cover/independent set.

title: Equality is Achievable
content: Axiomatizes that for every $n \ge 2$, there exists a graph achieving $\alpha_1 + \tau_1 = \lfloor n^2/4 \rfloor$. The balanced complete bipartite graph $K_{\lfloor n/2 \rfloor, \lceil n/2 \rceil}$ is triangle-free with $|E| = \lfloor n^2/4 \rfloor$.
mathContext: The bound $n^2/4$ is tight: $K_{\lfloor n/2 \rfloor, \lceil n/2 \rceil}$ achieves $\alpha_1 + \tau_1 = \lfloor n^2/4 \rfloor + 0 = \lfloor n^2/4 \rfloor$. Complete graphs and $K_{m,m}$ + universal vertex also achieve equality.

title: Problem #23 Conjecture: τ_B ≤ n²/25
content: Defines the conjecture from Erdős Problem #23: $\tau_B(G) \le n^2/25$ for all graphs on $n$ vertices. This would be a much stronger bound on bipartite removal than what follows from the EGT conjecture alone.
mathContext: Problem #23: $\tau_B(G) \le n^2/25$ for all $n$-vertex graphs. The constant $1/25$ comes from the extremal graph $C_5 \square K_{n/5}$ (a balanced blow-up of the 5-cycle), which has $\tau_B = n^2/25$.

title: Problem #23 Implies τ₁ Bound
content: If Problem #23 holds ($\tau_B \le n^2/25$), then $\tau_1 \le n^2/25$ via the chain $\tau_1 \le \tau_B \le n^2/25$. The proof uses `calc` with `Nat.cast_le` for the first step and the Problem #23 hypothesis for the second.
mathContext: $\tau_1(G) \le \tau_B(G) \le n^2/25$. Combined with Norin-Sun, this would give $\alpha_1(G) \ge n^2/4 - n^2/25 = 21n^2/100$, a strong lower bound on the sparse number.
